newsitem.title: UK: British NAAFI in financial services joint venture.
newsitem.headline: British NAAFI in financial services joint venture.

text.p: Britain's NAAFI, originally set up to feed the country's armed forces, has entered into a joint venture with HSBC Private Equity to provide financial services to Britain's armed forces.

NAAFI (Navy, Army and Air Force Institutes) said in a statement it was taking "a significant shareholding" in Warrior Group Limited and NAAFI's non-executive director Ian Lindsay would become chairman of the new company.

Bob Jones has been appointed as chief executive to lead the management team in partnership with NAAFI. HSBC Private Equity, part of the giant HSBC Holdings Plc group, led and structured the financing for the 104.2 million pound ($169.4 million) buy-in.

It was funded by a mix of debt and equity finance and further funds have been generated by the securitisation of NFS's existing loan book. NatWest Markets, the investment banking arm of National Westminster Bank Plc, led and arranged the 77.5 million pound securitisation and working capital facilities.
NAAFI said the deal would provide the new company "with the necessary financial backing and capital to expand its existing loan book and provide the opportunity to grow its business profitably".

Geoffrey Dart, NAAFI's chief executive, said the deal freed up substantial capital as it continued the restructuring and modernisation of its retail and leisure businesses but still provided a long-term income stream.
Dart said the shareholding in the new company demonstrated NAAFI's intention to deliver financial services to the armed forces "through partnerships with leading financial services companies".
NAAFI's turnover in 1995/96 was 411 million pounds and NFS had gross revenue of 18.0 million pounds in the same period, five percent of NAAFI's business.

Last month it said it would team up with retailer Spar to modernise its 200 stores. It said Spar would be its partner in a wide-ranging restructuring programme worth 500 million pounds over the next five years.
Spar will provide staff training and development, distribution and logistics and information technology as well as Spar branded goods.
NAAFI, which was formed in 1921 to provide canteen services to the navy, army and airforce, is moving away from supplying food to concentrate on shops and leisure, including bars.
Earlier this year it lost its traditional role of supplying canteens around the world for the British armed forces to food and distribution group Booker Group Plc.
It returned to profit in 1995/96 with a profit of 0.7 million pounds.
